title: Avoid degenerate triangles in PrimitiveMesh classes
body: Draft because this depends on PR #124169. ## What problem(s) does this PR solve? The current PrimitiveMesh classes have several cases of degenerate triangles. For example, at the poles of a SphereMesh, some of the triangles are fine, contributing to the visible surface of the mesh. Here's what it looks like when I export the mesh from Godot as a glTF file and inspect it in Blender: However, the other half of the pole triangles are degenerate, and contribute nothing: This PR fixes the degenerate cases, skipping all such degenerate triangles for SphereMesh, CapsuleMesh, and CylinderMesh, like this: For CapsuleMesh, the poles are fixed like SphereMesh, and also it will no longer have degenerate side triangles when the mid_height is zero. For CylinderMesh, it will no longer have degenerate triangles when one of the radius values is zero (creating a cone shape). This PR does not affect the visual appearance of the resulting meshes. I deliberately kept the existing geometry the same, for example not adjusting the texture coordinates. However, it does change the topology, and will affect user code that relied on that specific behavior, or depended on referencing specific elements of a PrimitiveMesh by index. I consider such usages to be "XKCD spacebar heating" problems, so I think it is not at all a problem to change this in a minor release of Godot, but I recommend NOT cherry-picking this PR to older branches. ## Additional information My motivation for making this PR is that in a 4D project I am using 3D meshes as input for some generation algorithms. An AI pointed out to me that the algorithm will break with some 3D meshes such as SphereMesh due to its degenerate triangles. I could also make my algorithm more robust, but regardless, this is a nice enhancement to Godot. It will slightly improve performance by skipping these degenerate triangles, and will make mesh operations less likely to error, such as calculating the normals of the resulting triangles. Every line of C++ in this PR is fully human-written: designed by a human mind, and typed by human fingers. However, I used AI to check my work and generate tests to search for degenerate triangles, it reports this is all of them.
